name: History trivia (medium)
description: 41 medium questions about world and US history, from ancient times to about 2000. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which French scholar announced in 1822 that he had deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs, using the Rosetta Stone as a key?
items.explain: Champollion accomplished the complete decipherment in 1822 after years of work. Young and Åkerblad made only partial progress.

source.title: Hieroglyphic writing - Rosetta Stone, Ancient Egypt, Decipherment | Britannica

items.question: The Rosetta Stone was found in 1799 by members of whose military expedition to Egypt?
items.explain: Members of Napoleon's expedition to Egypt found the stone near Rashid (Rosetta) on the Mediterranean coast.

source.title: Hieroglyphic writing - Rosetta Stone, Ancient Egypt, Decipherment | Britannica

items.question: The Rosetta Stone carries the same text in hieroglyphic, demotic and which other language?
items.explain: The stone has three scripts: hieroglyphic, demotic and Greek. Scholars could read the Greek, which gave them a way into the other two.

source.title: Hieroglyphic writing - Rosetta Stone, Ancient Egypt, Decipherment | Britannica

items.question: The text carved on the Rosetta Stone is a fairly mundane decree about the accomplishments of which ruler?
items.explain: The inscription turned out to be a decree honoring Ptolemy V Epiphanes, a Macedonian king of Egypt, not a store of ancient secrets.

source.title: French scholar announces he's cracked the Rosetta Stone code | HISTORY

items.question: Which Athenian general led the Greeks to victory over the Persians at the Battle of Marathon in 490 BCE?
items.explain: Miltiades the Younger led the Athenian forces to their decisive victory at Marathon. Themistocles is associated with Salamis, and Leonidas with Thermopylae.

source.title: Miltiades the Younger | Britannica

items.question: Which Greek city sent a smaller force to fight beside the Athenians at Marathon?
items.explain: Plataea fought alongside Athens at Marathon, honoring an alliance made in 519 BCE. The Spartans arrived only after the battle was over.

source.title: Ancient Greek civilization - Battle of Marathon, Athenians, Persians | Britannica

items.question: According to the traditional ancient accounts, about how many Persians died at Marathon, against only 192 Athenians?
items.explain: Britannica notes the Athenian victory was overwhelming, with 6,400 Persian casualties to 192 Athenian.

source.title: Ancient Greek civilization - Battle of Marathon, Athenians, Persians | Britannica

items.question: Which two men led the conspiracy that assassinated Julius Caesar in 44 BCE?
items.explain: The plot, involving some 60 men, was led by Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus. Antony and Octavian were Caesar's successors.

source.title: Julius Caesar | Britannica

items.question: After the civil wars that followed Caesar's assassination, his grand-nephew Octavian became the first Roman emperor under what name?
items.explain: Octavian emerged from the civil wars as Augustus, the first Roman emperor, and ended the Republic for good.

source.title: The Ides of March | HISTORY

items.question: Julius Caesar is said to have died from how many stab wounds when he was assassinated in the Senate?
items.explain: Accounts say the senators stabbed Caesar 23 times. About 60 men were in the conspiracy, which may tempt people to guess that number.

source.title: Julius Caesar's Assassination: Fall of the Roman Republic | HISTORY

items.question: At which meadow beside the River Thames did King John seal Magna Carta in June 1215?
items.explain: On 15 June 1215, King John set his seal to Magna Carta at Runnymede, facing rebellious barons.

source.title: Magna Carta | National Archives

items.question: Who annulled Magna Carta only about ten weeks after King John sealed it in 1215?
items.explain: Pope Innocent III nullified the agreement and England slid into civil war. Langton had helped draft the charter, and Henry III reissued it later.

source.title: Magna Carta | National Archives

items.question: Which English king issued the final, definitive version of Magna Carta in 1225?
items.explain: King John's son Henry III reissued the charter in 1225 in exchange for a new tax grant. His version, not John's, is the one that went into the statute book.

source.title: Magna Carta 1215: its social and political context | University of London Press

items.question: In which German city did Johannes Gutenberg set up his movable-type printing press around 1450?
items.explain: Gutenberg was from Mainz and developed his press there. The Gutenberg Museum stands opposite Mainz's cathedral.

source.title: Johannes Gutenberg | Wikipedia

items.question: Which famous book did Gutenberg complete printing in 1455?
items.explain: In 1455 Gutenberg completed his 42-line Bible, known as the Gutenberg Bible.

source.title: Johannes Gutenberg | Wikipedia

items.question: Traders from which Italian port city are traditionally said to have carried the plague from the Black Sea to Europe in the 1340s?
items.explain: The Black Death is thought to have entered Europe on Genoese trading ships sailing from the Black Sea.

source.title: Black Death | World History Encyclopedia

items.question: What share of Europe's population is commonly estimated to have died in the Black Death between 1347 and 1351?
items.explain: Britannica's timeline says the Black Death killed about one-third of Europe's people between 1347 and 1351. Historians still debate the exact figure.

source.title: Black Death Timeline | Britannica

items.question: The Black Death arrived in Europe in October 1347 at which Sicilian port?
items.explain: The second plague pandemic reached Messina, probably via Genoese ships, in October 1347. It then spread quickly across Europe.

source.title: History of the Plague: An Ancient Pandemic for the Age of COVID-19 | PMC

items.question: Which bacterium causes the plague that produced the Black Death?
items.explain: The Black Death's bacterial agent was Yersinia pestis, which still causes occasional outbreaks.

source.title: History of the Plague: An Ancient Pandemic for the Age of COVID-19 | PMC

items.question: In 1494 the Treaty of Tordesillas moved the dividing line farther west, letting Portugal claim the eastern coast of what is now which country?
items.explain: The 1494 treaty moved the Spanish-Portuguese line about 270 leagues west (the pope confirmed it in 1506), which let Portugal claim eastern Brazil.

source.title: Treaty of Tordesillas | National Geographic Education

items.question: Which Ottoman sultan conquered Constantinople in 1453?
items.explain: Sultan Mehmed II, later called the Conqueror, took the city on May 29, 1453, after a siege of about 55 days.

source.title: Fall of Constantinople | Britannica

items.question: The fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans in 1453 marked the end of which empire?
items.explain: Constantinople's capture ended the Byzantine Empire, the surviving eastern remnant of the Roman world.

source.title: Siege of Constantinople | Britannica

items.question: What did Mehmed II do with Hagia Sophia after capturing Constantinople?
items.explain: Mehmed II transformed the great church of Hagia Sophia into a mosque after the conquest.

source.title: Siege of Constantinople | Britannica

items.question: Which weapon did Mehmed II use to maintain a constant barrage on Constantinople's formidable walls in 1453?
items.explain: Mehmed II blockaded the city and used cannon to pound its walls until they were breached.

source.title: Fall of Constantinople | Britannica

items.question: The tea dumped into Boston Harbor in December 1773 belonged to which company?
items.explain: Patriots dumped 342 chests of tea belonging to the British East India Company, protesting the Tea Act of 1773.

source.title: Boston Tea Party | Britannica

items.question: Which Patriot leader organized the Boston Tea Party with about 60 members of the Sons of Liberty?
items.explain: After Governor Hutchinson refused to send the tea ships back, Samuel Adams organized the protest.

source.title: The Boston Tea Party | HISTORY

items.question: Which of these was one of the three ships whose tea was destroyed in the Boston Tea Party?
items.explain: The tea ships were the Dartmouth, the Eleanor and the Beaver, moored at Griffin's Wharf.

source.title: Boston Tea Party | Massachusetts Historical Society

items.question: What name did colonists give to the laws Parliament passed to punish Massachusetts after the Boston Tea Party?
items.explain: Shortly after the Tea Party, Parliament passed a set of punitive laws known as the Intolerable Acts to tighten control over the colonies.

source.title: 1773: The Boston Tea Party | Boston Public Library

items.question: Which French admiral's fleet controlled the Chesapeake Bay during the 1781 siege of Yorktown?
items.explain: Admiral de Grasse's fleet blocked access to Yorktown by sea, trapping Cornwallis's army. Rochambeau and Lafayette were army commanders.

source.title: Today in History - October 19 | Library of Congress

items.question: Which British prime minister reportedly cried out "Oh God, it is all over!" on hearing of the Yorktown surrender?
items.explain: Prime Minister Frederick North, Lord North, reacted this way to news of Cornwallis's surrender. Parliament moved toward ending the war in 1782.

source.title: Battle of Yorktown: Facts, Victory & Importance | HISTORY

items.question: How much did the United States pay France for the Louisiana Territory in 1803?
items.explain: Napoleon offered the entire territory for $15 million, far more than Jefferson's envoys were authorized to spend.

source.title: Louisiana Purchase, 1803 | Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State

items.question: What did Jefferson's envoys originally go to Paris in 1803 to try to buy from France?
items.explain: Jefferson wanted New Orleans and nearby land for American access to the Mississippi. Napoleon surprised the envoys by offering all of Louisiana.

source.title: Louisiana Purchase | Council on Foreign Relations

items.question: Which future U.S. president did Jefferson send to Paris to join Robert Livingston in negotiating for New Orleans in 1803?
items.explain: Jefferson sent James Monroe to join Livingston, and the two accepted Napoleon's offer of the whole territory.

source.title: Louisiana Purchase, 1803 | Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State

items.question: Which Prussian field marshal's army arrived late in the day to help Wellington defeat Napoleon at Waterloo?
items.explain: Blücher's Prussians reached the field and attacked Napoleon's flank, completing the French defeat. Ney and Grouchy were French marshals.

source.title: Battle of Waterloo | Britannica

items.question: What is the name of the period from Napoleon's escape from exile to his defeat at Waterloo?
items.explain: Waterloo took place during the Hundred Days, the period from Napoleon's escape from Elba to the return of Louis XVIII.

source.title: Battle of Waterloo | Britannica

items.question: Which enslaved people did Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation of January 1, 1863 declare free?
answers: Those in the loyal border states
items.explain: The proclamation covered only the seceded states and left slavery untouched in the loyal border states. Its promise depended on Union military victory.

source.title: Information on the Emancipation Proclamation | National Archives

items.question: Besides declaring freedom in rebel states, what else did the Emancipation Proclamation announce?
answers: Black men would join the Union military
Rebel officers would receive full pardons
Slaveholders would be paid for losses
Foreign volunteers could join Union units
items.correct: Black men would join the Union military
items.explain: The proclamation announced that Black men would be accepted into the Union army and navy. Almost 200,000 served by the war's end.

source.title: Information on the Emancipation Proclamation | National Archives

items.question: Which famous orator spoke for about two hours before Lincoln gave his two-minute Gettysburg Address?
items.explain: Edward Everett was the featured speaker at the cemetery dedication on November 19, 1863. Lincoln's remarks lasted only about two minutes.

source.title: The Gettysburg Address (1863) | National Constitution Center

items.question: In the Gettysburg Address, Lincoln's phrase "four score and seven years ago" pointed back to which year?
items.explain: A score is 20, so 87 years before 1863 is 1776, the year of the Declaration of Independence.

source.title: Gettysburg Address: 1863 | Ben's Guide to the U.S. Government (GPO)

items.question: The Meiji Restoration of 1868 overthrew which ruling regime in Japan?
items.explain: Activists overthrew the Tokugawa family, which had ruled Japan for more than 260 years, and restored imperial power.

source.title: Meiji Restoration | World History Encyclopedia

items.question: The reign title "Meiji", adopted by Emperor Mutsuhito in 1868, means what in English?
items.explain: After the Tokugawa were overthrown, Mutsuhito adopted the reign title Meiji, meaning "enlightened rule".

source.title: Meiji Restoration | World History Encyclopedia
